questions.q: What does boredom do for the brain, according to the summary?
a: It gives the brain rest and space to generate new ideas
It shuts down unnecessary cognitive functions
It increases focus by removing distractions
It stores memories more efficiently
questions.why: White space lets the mind reset and wander, which is where ideas emerge.

questions.q: What does the summary say boredom allowed early humans to do?
a: Think beyond survival and create new things
Develop language more quickly
Cooperate in larger hunting groups
Remember dangerous places for longer
questions.why: Boredom is presented as part of human evolution, not a sign of laziness.

questions.q: Which type of daydreaming does the summary recommend practicing?
a: Positive-constructive daydreaming
Poor attention control
Guilty-dysphoric daydreaming
Anxious-avoidant daydreaming
questions.why: It is the only one of the three types that produces useful, healthy mind output.

a: The mind drifts into negative, self-critical thoughts
The mind jumps rapidly between unrelated tasks
The mind replays happy memories in detail
The mind plans practical steps toward a goal
questions.why: This type diminishes joy and increases stress rather than producing ideas.

questions.q: Which rule does the summary offer for breaking a phone habit?
a: You cannot use your phone while moving
You cannot check your phone before noon
You must delete every social app each week
You must leave your phone in another room at night
questions.why: The challenge pairs that rule with stopping meaningless photos and deleting the worst app.
